related_synthesis_entries.claim: For higher derivatives, the proof no longer has simple logarithmic derivatives or stable real-part signs, so it constructs nonvanishing regions and reconciles separately normalized logarithms on a connected domain before contour integration.
related_synthesis_entries.limit: The construction is RH-conditional and constants depend on the fixed derivative order.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The lemma constructs one connected zero-free region on which three logarithms can be chosen coherently. Far-right normalization, far-left functional-equation asymptotics, and RH-based absence of derivative zeros are coordinated by a carefully selected height tk.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: Under RH, constants ak, σk, and tk are chosen so Gk is close to 1 on the right, a functional-equation remainder is small on the left, F^(k)/F and ζ^(k)/ζ are nonzero with bounded argument on σk≤σ<1/2 above tk−1, and neither ζ nor ζ^(k) vanishes along the horizontal line at tk. Stirling-type estimates control F derivatives, while RH gives only finitely many off-line zeros of each ζ^(j).
directed.conceptual_reading: Nonvanishing is used as branch infrastructure: once ratios avoid zero on a connected region, local argument choices telescope into global holomorphic logarithms suitable for contour integration.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The ratios F^(j)/F^(j−1) and ζ^(j)/ζ^(j−1), together with the common strip and height tk, bridge functional-equation asymptotics to compatible logarithmic branches.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The construction assumes RH and depends on unspecified sufficiently large constants. It proves existence, not effective numerical values for ak, σk, or tk.
directed.uncertainty: Exact angle intervals and derivative-ratio formulas are notation-sensitive and should be checked against the PDF.

supported: Lemma 2.1 directly supports far-right control of G_k, far-left functional-equation estimates, nonvanishing and argument ranges for F^(k)/F and zeta^(k)/zeta in the left strip, and selection of a horizontal height avoiding zeros.
inference: Using nonvanishing as branch infrastructure and telescoping successive zeta-derivative ratios is a reasonable interpretation of conditions 3 and 4.
unsupported_or_imported: The spontaneous claim that one connected zero-free region supports three coherently chosen logarithms overstates the span: G_k is controlled on a far-right half-plane, while the two ratio logarithms are constructed on the strip sigma_k<=sigma<1/2; no single common region spanning these is established here.
paraphrase_or_style_risk: Branch-infrastructure language is useful only if the distinct domains and distinct logarithms are not blurred into a generic coherence story.
context_or_ocr_risk: Derivative ratios, parity-dependent angle intervals, and thresholds are formula-sensitive, though this text layer is substantially cleaner than Atkinson's.
missed_mechanism: The height t_k is chosen to satisfy five separate conditions, and the horizontal-line nonvanishing uses the identity theorem after other zero-free ranges are assembled.
revision_instructions: Separate the far-right G_k normalization from the connected left-strip logarithmic branches; state only that a common t_k coordinates their later use, not that all three live on one zero-free domain.

unit_result_entry.title: The normalized derivative argument, not the zeta argument, sets the present counting error
unit_result_entry.why_material: Completing Proposition 3.1 expresses the zero count through two critical-line arguments; RH bounds make the normalized derivative term larger, and the final comparison with the classical S(T) formula identifies both the quantitative bottleneck and the unknown implied constant.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Subtracting adjacent Littlewood rectangles isolates the total number of derivative zeros
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: The immutable v1 span applies Littlewood's lemma at two nearby left boundaries, cancels the weighted real-part information, and reduces the count to main terms plus averaged zeta and normalized-derivative arguments at the critical line.

related_synthesis_entries.claim: Littlewood's lemma leaves a normalized-derivative argument integral in the weighted real-part formula, and shrinking the difference of two rectangles turns the same boundary information into the total count; its best current bound therefore fixes both error scales.
related_synthesis_entries.limit: The two results use different functionals of the argument, and the source does not prove the expected sharper bound.
related_synthesis_entries.title: One boundary argument controls both horizontal displacement and total zero count

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The zero count separates into the classical zeta argument and a normalized derivative argument. Under RH the latter has the weaker bound, so it alone determines the present error scale and is the concrete target for improvement.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: The source obtains Nk(T)=T/(2π)log(T/(4π))−T/(2π)+(1/(2π))arg Gk(1/2+iT)+(1/(2π))arg ζ(1/2+iT)+O_k(1). RH gives arg ζ=O(log T/log log T) but only arg Gk=O_k(log T/(log log T)^(1/2)); perturbation handles exceptional ordinates, yielding the latter scale for the zero-count error.
directed.conceptual_reading: Normalizing ζ^(k) into Gk isolates what differentiation adds beyond ordinary zeta zero counting. Comparing the two argument bounds diagnoses the formal-worker bottleneck rather than hiding it in one aggregate O-term.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The two critical-line arguments in Proposition 3.1 are the bridge from analytic function values to the counting function Nk(T).
directed.boundary_or_failure: The bound is best known in the source, not claimed optimal, and no useful estimate for its implied constant is available. All conclusions assume RH.
directed.uncertainty: The hierarchy of errors is clear; argument branch normalizations should be checked for exact reuse.

supported: The zero-count formula, the two critical-line argument bounds under RH, exceptional-height perturbation, comparison with S(T), best-known status, and unknown implied constant for arg G_k are explicit.
inference: Normalizing zeta^(k) as G_k to separate the derivative-specific argument from the classical zeta argument is a useful source-grounded reading.
unsupported_or_imported: The phrase formal-worker bottleneck is imported Mathia/prover terminology and is mathematically inapplicable here; the unit diagnoses an analytic argument-bound bottleneck, not a formal solver.
paraphrase_or_style_risk: Most content is specific, but importing project jargon risks turning a precise analytic limitation into generic systems prose.
context_or_ocr_risk: Argument normalizations and exact error scales are formula-sensitive, though their hierarchy is clear.
missed_mechanism: The larger of the two argument bounds dominates after direct substitution into Proposition 3.1; this elementary maximum, not an external worker model, explains the error.
revision_instructions: Replace formal-worker bottleneck with analytic bottleneck in controlling arg G_k(1/2+iT), and preserve the source's no-optimality and unknown-constant caveats.
